data.one_liner: Key-value store abstraction with caching semantics and pluggable backends.
data.what_it_does: Provides a key-value storage abstraction with plain vault semantics and advanced cache-driven semantics. It supports multiple eviction and expiration policies, binary serialization, events, and a pluggable backend architecture.
use_when: You need advanced caching semantics like expiration and eviction policies.
You want a unified key-value abstraction that can swap storage backends easily.
You need tiered caching with an in-memory primary cache and secondary persistent storage.
avoid_when: You need a full relational database with complex queries and joins.
You only want simple preferences without any caching features and prefer a lighter direct dependency.
strengths: Rich caching features including multiple expiry and eviction policies (LRU, LFU, FIFO, etc.).
Pluggable backend architecture supporting memory, file, SQLite, Hive, and more.
weaknesses: Requires adding both the core API package and a separate storage provider package.
API surface can be complex due to many configuration options and policies.
data.setup_notes: Add stash and your chosen storage implementation (e.g., stash_memory) to pubspec.yaml.

alternatives.name: hive_ce
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you want a lightweight standalone NoSQL database without the abstraction layer overhead of Stash.

alternatives.name: shared_preferences
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you only need simple key-value storage for basic app settings.
